newsitem.title: USA: Merck profits jump in first quarter.
newsitem.headline: Merck profits jump in first quarter.

text.p: Merck & Co. Inc. said Wednesday its profits jumped 18 percent in the first quarter as demand for its established pharmaceutical products grew worldwide.

Merck earned $1.02 billion, or 84 cents a share, in the quarter ended March 31, up from $863.8 million, or 70 cents a share, in the year-ago period. This slightly exceeded the consensus estimate of 83 cents a share.
Sales rose 23 percent to $5.6 billion from $4.5 billion.
"Sales growth for the quarter was led by established major products, recent product introductions and growth from the Merck-Medco Managed Care business," said Chairman Raymond Gilmartin.
"Both our domestic and international operations reported strong unit volume gains."
Profit growth was driven by strong unit volume gains, while foreign exchange cut sales growth by 1 percentage point.

Merck's products include Pepcid, a prescription drug for duodenal ulcers; Vasotec for high blood pressure; Crixivan for the treatment of HIV infection in adults; and Fosamax, a breakthrough nonhormonal medicine for the treatment of osteoporosis in postmenopausal women.

The company, based in Whitehouse Station, N.J., said the unfavourable effects of inflation and currency exchange were partially offset by cost controls and productivity improvements in manufacturing, selling and general and administrative expenses.
Merck's stock rose $1 to $85.50 on the New York Stock Exchange in early afternoon trading.
